doc.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Basie, Ellington and Lunceford as models
summary: Basie for swing, Ellington for harmony and creativity, Lunceford among the best; Snooky Young bridged them.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Was the Basie group a standard for your guys to listen to? I mean was it—
Well for swinging, yeah. I mean Duke’s band was another think, the Duke for harmony I guess.
But for out and out swing.
That and the Jimmie Lunceford band was an awful good swinging band.
Those are two names that keep coming up.
The best I would say. That and Basie.
Have you talked to Snooky or do you plan to?
Yeah. We had a nice conversation.
Yeah. Because he was with Lunceford and Basie. That’s a lot of history there.
Yeah, well they were just special. A special time and a bunch of special people came together I think.
